correctness.rationale: For the 20 binary weight-three words of length six, deletion shadow intersecting H={00011,00110,01100,10101,11000} has exactly one element, partitioning the words into five four-word bins. Pairwise disjoint deletion shadows force at most one codeword per bin, proving |C|≤5, and the exhibited five-word code attains equality. Independently generated all 20 length-six weight-three words, all 190 pairwise shadow collisions (cross-checked via LCS), enumerated every C(20,5)=15504 candidate maximum code, and obtained exactly 8. Under reversal and complement their 4 two-element orbits are all fixed by reverse-complement; four union shadows contain 18 words and four all 20 words. Since no six-code can cross the five-bin bound, this is complete, not sampling or an inference from a timeout.

value.rationale: The balanced middle layer n=6, weight=3 is a natural small constant-weight deletion graph whose extremal codebook geometry, natural reversal/complement action and perfect received-layer partitions merit an exact classification. The complete extremizer/coverage orbit census is a mathematically natural finite invariant needed to compare constant-weight deletion code constructions; it is not the unrestricted code optimum or a mere chromatic-coloring restatement. The parameter is narrow, and broader consequences are not claimed.

limitations: Only n=6 weight3 one-deletion case; symmetry is the specified order-four reversal/complement group, not full automorphism group.
